get.description:
Redirects to the provider's sign-in page, or to `/signin?error=failed` when sign-in
with it is not available or this address made too many sign-in requests in a minute. A
provider's account that never signed in joins the CandleStack user with its email, so the
email links a user's GitHub and Google; it signs in to a new user when no user has it.

With `intent=connect` (signed in, a link of Settings) the provider's account is added to
the signed-in user's sign-in methods instead: the callback returns to `next` (default
`/settings/sign-in`), or to `/settings/sign-in?error=taken` when that account already
signs in to another CandleStack user, or `/settings/sign-in?error=failed`, also right away
when the request does not come from the app's own pages.

get.description:
Everything the Dashboard shows: the counts of the user's backtests, the newest ones,
the best finished ones by Sharpe ratio, return, drawdown and win rate, and the best
starred ones.

Searches the instruments of both markets: every Binance spot pair that is trading and
every active tradable US stock and ETF at Alpaca (without OTC). Each item carries its last
price, 24 h change and 24 h volume in USD, refreshed every few minutes, its last 10 daily
candles (`spark`), refreshed once a day (null without them), and the open time of its first
candle (`available_from`, null while not known yet).

Ranking: the top pair of a crypto base asset equal to the query (`btc` finds `BTCUSDT`
first), exact symbol, the other pairs of that base asset, symbol prefix, prefix of a word
in the name, substring of the symbol, substring of the name; ties go to `sort`, then to the
shorter symbol, then alphabetically. Without `q`, every instrument comes back in `sort`:
the most traded first by default.
`exchange` narrows any of these to the instruments that trade on it.
`total` counts all matches: page through them with `offset` and `limit`.

When the instrument list of one market cannot be loaded, the other market is still
searched and `unavailable` names the missing one; 503 when no market can be searched.

Uploads a model file: the body is the file, `name` its file name. The file is checked
before it is kept: `opens` (a real Keras model with no custom code inside, nothing from
the file is executed) and `weights` (it holds trained weights). A file with a name the user
already has gets a number, as `lstm (2).keras`.

409.description: The file does not fit into the user's storage (`storage-full`; `used_bytes` and `quota_bytes` say how much is taken), the user has 100 models already (`too-many-models`; `limit`), another upload of the user is in progress (`upload-in-progress`), or, rarely, the numbered name the file got is one the user has in another case (`model-name-taken`).

413.description: The file is larger than 50 MB (`model-too-large`).

415.description: Not a format the app takes yet, only Keras (`.keras`) for now (`unsupported-model-format`).

422.description: A check failed (`model-check-failed`): `check` names it (`opens` or `weights`) and `detail` says why; or the request is invalid (`validation`).

delete.description: Deletes the model and its file, which frees its storage.

get.description:
Every block a model's manifest can name, by step (representation, feature,
normalization, window): its versioned id, what it does, its warm-up and its parameters
with their types, ranges and defaults. The app builds the manifest form from it. A block
that is not listed yet makes a manifest that cannot run.
